edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 in immediately available funds as consideration for the Shares.

2. Closing. Subject to satisfaction or waiver of the conditions to Closing set forth in this Agreement, Closing shall occur within 30 days after the date of this Agreement, or at such other time as the parties may agree in writing.

3. Representations. The Seller represents that, to the Seller’s knowledge, the financial statements delivered to the Buyer have been prepared in accordance with the accounting principles stated therein and are accurate in all material respects.

4. Confidentiality. The parties shall keep the existence and terms of this Agreement confidential, except that either party may disclose them to its affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, financing sources, and professional advisers who are bound by confidentiality obligations, or as required by law, regulation, or a competent authority. A party required to make a disclosure shall, to the extent legally permitted, give the other party advance notice and reasonably cooperate in seeking confidential treatment.

Please also revise the confidentiality clause to permit disclosure to the Buyer’s actual and prospective financing sources and their advisers, and to the extent reasonably necessary for the Buyer’s internal approval process, in each case subject to appropriate confidentiality protections.

Please provide a revised draft incorporating the changes set out above. The Buyer’s proposal is for discussion and remains subject to diligence and definitive documentation.

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The aggregate purchase price for the Shares shall be USD 42,000,000 (the “Base Purchase Price”), subject to adjustment at Closing, dollar-for-dollar, for (a) cash of the Company as of Closing, added to the Base Purchase Price; (b) indebtedness of the Company as of Closing, deducted from the Base Purchase Price; (c) unpaid transaction expenses of the Company or Seller for which the Company is responsible, deducted from the Base Purchase Price; and (d) the amount by which Closing Working Capital exceeds the agreed working-capital target, added to the Base Purchase Price, or falls below that target, deducted from the Base Purchase Price. The parties shall agree in the definitive agreement on the working-capital target, accounting principles, calculation procedures, and a post-Closing review and dispute-resolution process. No item shall be counted more than once. The adjusted purchase price shall be paid at Closing in immediately available funds, subject to any agreed escrow or other customary holdback expressly set forth in the definitive agreement.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 30 days after execution of the definitive agreement, or at such other time as the parties agree in writing, subject to: (a) completion by Buyer of its confirmatory due diligence, with no matter identified that would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the Company; (b) execution and delivery of mutually agreed definitive ancillary documents; (c) accuracy in all material respects of the parties’ representations and warranties, subject to agreed materiality and other qualifiers, and performance in all material respects of their covenants; (d) receipt of required governmental and third-party approvals and expiration or termination of applicable waiting periods; and (e) other customary closing conditions to be set forth in the definitive agreement. Buyer shall conduct diligence promptly and in good faith and shall notify Seller promptly of any material diligence concern. Neither party shall be required to close unless the applicable conditions are satisfied or waived in writing.

3. Seller Representations. In the definitive agreement, Seller shall make customary representations and warranties, subject to negotiated qualifications, exceptions, and disclosure schedules, concerning: (a) Seller’s organization, authority, and enforceability; (b) the Company’s organization and authority; (c) capitalization, ownership of and good title to the Shares, free of liens created by Seller; (d) the financial statements delivered to Buyer, prepared in accordance with the accounting principles stated therein and fairly presenting in all material respects the financial condition and results reflected therein; (e) absence of undisclosed liabilities, subject to customary exceptions for liabilities reflected or reserved in the financial statements, incurred in the ordinary course since their date, or otherwise disclosed; (f) material contracts; (g) compliance with applicable law; (h) litigation; (i) taxes; (j) employees and employee benefit matters; and (k) brokers. The scope of each representation, including knowledge, materiality, time-period, and ordinary-course qualifications, and the contents of the disclosure schedules, shall be negotiated in the definitive agreement. No representation or warranty shall be made except as expressly set forth in that agreement.

4. Confidentiality. The parties shall keep the existence and terms of this Agreement and information exchanged in connection with the transaction confidential, except that either party may disclose such information to its affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, financing sources, and professional advisers who need to know it and are bound by confidentiality obligations or professional duties of confidentiality. Buyer may also disclose such information to its actual and prospective financing sources and their respective advisers, and to its representatives to the extent reasonably necessary for Buyer’s internal approval process, in each case subject to confidentiality protections at least as protective as those set forth herein. A party may disclose information as required by law, regulation, or a competent authority. To the extent legally permitted, a party required to make a disclosure shall give the other party advance notice and reasonably cooperate in seeking confidential treatment. Each party is responsible for compliance with this Section by persons to whom it discloses information.

5. Indemnification. The definitive agreement shall provide customary indemnification for breaches of representations, warranties, covenants, and other specified obligations, subject to negotiated limitations, including an agreed survival period, deductible or tipping basket, cap, and customary exclusions and procedures. Fundamental representations and specified matters may be subject to separately negotiated survival periods and limits. The parties shall address mitigation, recoveries from insurance or third parties, and the prohibition on double recovery. Except for fraud and any other expressly negotiated exceptions, the agreed indemnification provisions shall be the parties’ exclusive remedy for claims arising out of the definitive agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby.

6. Covenants and Remedies. The definitive agreement shall include customary interim operating covenants, including an obligation for Seller to cause the Company to operate in the ordinary course between signing and Closing, subject to agreed exceptions and Buyer’s consent rights, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. It shall also include customary efforts, access, cooperation, and transaction-announcement covenants. Remedies for breach shall be as set forth in the definitive agreement, including any agreed right to seek specific performance and the indemnification remedies and limitations described therein.
